requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.
rationale:
The subject is a content requirement for the `instructions` string. It has four parts. The instructions tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting. They explain how to select the tags of excerpts used as evidence. They explain how to pass `used: []` when none contributed. They state that finishing records the selected inputs without fetching more source.

One test is marked for this requirement: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`. It covers the four parts as follows:
- **Content assertions.** The test runs `search_text` for "absent", which returns an empty result. It parses the returned `instructions` and asserts that it contains each of these phrases:
  - "Before submitting, close every delivered search page". This covers the instruction to finish every delivered page before submitting.
  - "finish_search". This names the tool.
  - "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read". This covers how to select tags of evidence excerpts.
  - "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result". This covers passing an empty `used` when nothing contributed.
  - "without reading more source". This covers the point that finishing records inputs without fetching more source.
- **Both search kinds.** A fresh `search_text` result carries the same `instructions` string, checked with `assert_eq!(hits["instructions"], instructions)`. The first successful `search_structure` result from a peer session also carries the same string, checked with `assert_eq!(page["instructions"], instructions)`. So the content holds for text and structural searches.
- **Behaviour the instructions describe.** The test also runs `finish_search` with `used: []` and with a selected tag. The selected tag yields the expected `Dependency::Node`. The empty list yields no dependencies, and the response is `finished: true`. This matches the instructions' claims about selecting tags and about `used: []`.

Delivery rules (first search only, omitted on later and continuation pages, failed searches) belong to the parent `first_search.instructions` requirement. They are tested here too, but they are not obligations of this subject.

The assertions are substring checks on the specific content the requirement lists, so they would catch removal or alteration of any of the four parts. I found no gap.
